slot.brief: Alkyl halide undergoes dehydrohalogenation with alcoholic KOH, then the alkene is treated with HBr in absence of peroxide; ask for the major final product considering Markovnikov addition.

stem: On heating 1-bromo-2-methylpropane with alcoholic $\text{KOH}$, then treating the alkene with $\text{HBr}$ in the absence of peroxide, the major product is:

verdicts.working: Alcoholic KOH eliminates HBr from 1-bromo-2-methylpropane to form 2-methylpropene. HBr adds without peroxide by Markovnikov addition, giving 2-bromo-2-methylpropane.

working:
$\text{(CH}_3)_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{Br} \rightarrow \text{CH}_2=\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)_2$; Markovnikov addition of $\text{HBr}$ gives $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CBr}$, 2-bromo-2-methylpropane.

Independent check: Alcoholic KOH eliminates HBr from 1-bromo-2-methylpropane to form 2-methylpropene. HBr adds without peroxide by Markovnikov addition, giving 2-bromo-2-methylpropane.
solution:
Alcoholic KOH causes β-elimination to form 2-methylpropene:
$$\text{(CH}_3)_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{Br} \xrightarrow{\text{alc. KOH}} \text{CH}_2=\text{C(CH}_3)_2$$
In the absence of peroxide, HBr adds by Markovnikov’s rule, placing Br on the more substituted carbon to give $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CBr}$, 2-bromo-2-methylpropane.
